raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
- Install EFA 1.51.0 (minimal: libfabric, aws-ofi-nccl, hwloc) in vllm-openai-base when INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true.
- Drop the EFA Mooncake wheel swap; mooncake-transfer-engine 0.3.14 includes the EFA transport.
- Rename Dockerfile.efa to Dockerfile.deepep_efa. It now only rebuilds DeepEP for GIN over EFA and sets the aws-ofi-nccl NCCL plugins. IMAGE_USER restores the base's user for non-root bases.
- Rename the release images and publish target from -efa to -deepep-efa.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
Let's keep the variant called `efa`, currently it's just for supporting DeepEP, but it can be used later for other changes that can't go into the main container.

+# Install the AWS EFA userspace with the KV connectors: NIXL's LIBFABRIC plugin
+# and Mooncake's EFA transport load libfabric at runtime.
+RUN if [ "$INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS" = "true" ]; then \
+        set -eux; \
+        EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE="/tmp/aws-efa-installer-${EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION}.tar.gz"; \
+        curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors \
+            "https://efa-installer.amazonaws.com/aws-efa-installer-${EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION}.tar.gz" \
+            -o "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}"; \
+        echo "${EFA_INSTALLER_SHA256}  ${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" | sha256sum -c -; \
+        tar -xzf "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" -C /tmp; \
+        # The installer apt-installs dependencies; earlier layers purged the lists.
+        apt-get update -y; \
+        # Minimal install: libfabric, aws-ofi-nccl and hwloc only. --build-ngc
+        # implies --skip-kmod --skip-limit-conf --no-verify.
+        (cd /tmp/aws-efa-installer && \
+            ./efa_installer.sh --skip-mpi --skip-rdma-core --build-ngc); \
+        test -x /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info; \
+        /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info --version; \
+        # `-l` lists providers without EFA hardware, so this works in a build.
+        /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info -l | grep -q '^efa:'; \
+        EFA_NIXL_PLUGIN=$(find /usr/local/lib -name libplugin_LIBFABRIC.so \
+            -print -quit); \
+        test -n "${EFA_NIXL_PLUGIN}"; \
+        ldd "${EFA_NIXL_PLUGIN}" | grep -q 'libfabric\.so\.1 => /opt/amazon/efa/lib/'; \
+        # Plugins that NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi and NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=ofi resolve to.
+        ldconfig -p | grep -q '/opt/amazon/ofi-nccl/lib/libnccl-net-ofi\.so$'; \
+        ldconfig -p | grep -q '/opt/amazon/ofi-nccl/lib/libnccl-tuner-ofi\.so$'; \
+        apt-get clean; \
+        rm -rf "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" /tmp/aws-efa-installer \
+            /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
+    fi
 # Mooncake registers GPU memory for RDMA via nvidia-peermem by default. Hosts

@@ -0,0 +1,102 @@
+# DeepEP for AWS EFA on top of a vllm-openai image: rebuilds DeepEP from the
+# amazon-contributing fork, whose deepep_v2 backend carries EP traffic over EFA
+# through NCCL GIN, and routes NCCL over aws-ofi-nccl. Published as *-deepep-efa.
+#
+# The base must be built with INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true, which installs the
+# AWS EFA userspace (libfabric, aws-ofi-nccl):
+#   docker build -f docker/Dockerfile.deepep_efa \
+#       --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=vllm/vllm-openai:latest -t vllm:openai-deepep-efa docker/
+#
+# For a vllm-openai-nonroot base, also pass --build-arg IMAGE_USER=vllm.
+#
+# The host still provides the EFA kernel module and memlock limits.
+ARG BASE_IMAGE=vllm/vllm-openai:latest
+FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}
+
+# The user the image runs as, restored after the root-only build steps below.
+# Docker cannot read the base's USER at build time, so check it matches.
+ARG IMAGE_USER=root
+RUN if [ "$(id -un)" != "${IMAGE_USER}" ]; then \
+        echo "Base image runs as '$(id -un)'; rebuild with \
+--build-arg IMAGE_USER=$(id -un)" >&2; \
+        exit 1; \
+    fi
+USER root
+
+# DeepEP GIN uses NCCL over EFA, so the base must already have aws-ofi-nccl.
+RUN set -eu; \
+    if ! ldconfig -p | grep -q '/opt/amazon/ofi-nccl/lib/libnccl-net-ofi\.so$'; then \
+        echo "Dockerfile.deepep_efa needs a base image built with \
+--build-arg INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true (no aws-ofi-nccl found)" >&2; \
+        exit 1; \
+    fi
+
+# Route NCCL over EFA. Override with `-e NCCL_NET_PLUGIN= -e NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=`
+# to run this image on a non-EFA host.
+ENV NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi \
+    NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=ofi
+
+# Replace the base image's upstream DeepEP with the amazon-contributing fork.
+ARG DEEPEP_REPO="https://github.com/amazon-contributing/DeepEP.git"
+ARG DEEPEP_REF="874779c9ccd2294b56304bd6cc5f138f1f71d097"
+ARG DEEPEP_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="9.0a;10.0a;10.3a"
+
+# Headers and git for DeepEP's nvcc build. `reinstall` also installs packages
+# that are absent.
+RUN set -eux; \
+    CUDA_PKG_VERSION=$(nvcc --version \
+        | grep -oP 'release \K[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | tr '.' '-'); \
+    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get update -y; \
+    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get reinstall -y --no-install-recommends \
+        git \
+        libcusparse-dev-${CUDA_PKG_VERSION} \
+        libcusolver-dev-${CUDA_PKG_VERSION} \
+        cuda-nvrtc-dev-${CUDA_PKG_VERSION}; \
+    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/opt/uv/cache \
+    set -eux; \
+    git clone "${DEEPEP_REPO}" /tmp/deepep; \
+    cd /tmp/deepep; \
+    git checkout "${DEEPEP_REF}"; \
+    git submodule update --init --recursive; \
+    uv pip uninstall --system deep_ep 2>/dev/null || true; \
+    NCCL_ROOT="$(python3 -c "import importlib.util, os; \
+s = importlib.util.find_spec('nvidia.nccl'); \
+print(os.path.dirname(s.origin or s.submodule_search_locations[0]))")/nccl"; \
+    export EP_NCCL_ROOT_DIR="${NCCL_ROOT}"; \
+    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${NCCL_ROOT}/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"; \
+    # The CUDA driver stubs let DeepEP link libcuda in a builder with no driver.
+    export LIBRARY_PATH="${NCCL_ROOT}/lib:/usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs:\
+/usr/local/cuda/targets/x86_64-linux/lib/stubs:${LIBRARY_PATH:-}"; \
+    export DISABLE_AGGRESSIVE_PTX_INSTRS=1; \
+    export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="${DEEPEP_CUDA_ARCH_LIST}"; \
+    uv pip install --system --no-deps -vv --no-build-isolation .; \
+    cd /; \
+    rm -rf /tmp/deepep; \
+    # vLLM only logs when the deepep_v2 backend is unavailable, so fail here.
+    python3 -c "import deep_ep; assert hasattr(deep_ep, 'ElasticBuffer'), \
+'DeepEP built without the ElasticBuffer (v2) API'"
+
+USER ${IMAGE_USER}
+
+# Provenance. Build args from docker-build-metadata-args.sh override the values
+# inherited from the base image; without them the base's values are kept.
+ARG BASE_IMAGE
+ARG VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT
+ARG VLLM_BUILD_PIPELINE
+ARG VLLM_BUILD_URL
+ARG VLLM_IMAGE_TAG
+ENV VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT=${VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT} \
+    VLLM_BUILD_PIPELINE=${VLLM_BUILD_PIPELINE} \
+    VLLM_BUILD_URL=${VLLM_BUILD_URL} \
+    VLLM_IMAGE_TAG=${VLLM_IMAGE_TAG}
+LABEL org.opencontainers.image.revision="${VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT}" \
+      org.opencontainers.image.version="${VLLM_IMAGE_TAG}" \
+      org.opencontainers.image.url="${VLLM_BUILD_URL}" \
+      ai.vllm.build.commit="${VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT}" \
+      ai.vllm.build.pipeline="${VLLM_BUILD_PIPELINE}" \
+      ai.vllm.build.url="${VLLM_BUILD_URL}" \
+      ai.vllm.image.tag="${VLLM_IMAGE_TAG}" \
+      ai.vllm.deepep-efa.base-image="${BASE_IMAGE}" \
+      ai.vllm.deepep-efa.deepep-ref="${DEEPEP_REF}"

+When `INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true`, `vllm-openai-base` also installs a minimal
+AWS EFA userspace (libfabric, aws-ofi-nccl and hwloc), which NIXL's LIBFABRIC
+backend and Mooncake's EFA transport load at runtime. Kernel modules and host
+limits remain host-managed.
 
 The image does not change vLLM's Mooncake protocol default (`rdma`). To use
 EFA, set it per connector:
 
 - `MooncakeConnector`: `"mooncake_protocol": "efa"` in `kv_connector_extra_config`.
 - `MooncakeStoreConnector`: `"protocol": "efa"` in the JSON file at `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`.
